info.name: Hummingbird — Rental Flow (Mariposa)
info.description:
The eleven documented rental-flow calls, plus the extras we found by probing.

EVERY request signs itself: a collection-level pre-request script sets `epoch` to the current unix time, so `x-storageapi-date` is always fresh. You never set it by hand.

RESPONSES FEED THE NEXT CALL. Each request's Tests tab writes the ids it returns into collection variables — hold a unit and `holdToken` fills in, finalize documents and `docSrc`/`docVersion` fill in — so the chain runs top to bottom without copy-paste.

ORDER MATTERS. 5 Hold → 7 Lease set-up → 9 Documents → 10 Lease → 11 Autopay is the rental. A hold lasts 15 minutes; past that, re-run 5.

WATCH OUT: 9 and 10 create a REAL lease and take a REAL payment, even in the sandbox. 10 puts the unit out of inventory permanently.

VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against edge.tenant.dev.

exec: // x-storageapi-date must be the CURRENT unix time on every request —
// a stale one is rejected. Set here so no request carries it by hand.

variable.description: The guide says prod.edge.tenant.dev; this host is the one our key works against.
OUR application id. TenantInc's sample curl uses appc02fcbc01b5e41818669077c87c01e7f, which answers 'I was unable to find that application' for this key.
Storage Outlet. On a published site this comes from the Company collection.
A tier_id from request 3. Filled automatically.
Filled by request 4b — required by request 9.
Non-prorated monthly rent. Filled by request 7.
Filled by request 7 from invoice.balance (NET), not total_due (gross).
The tenant's gate PIN. Filled by request 10 — the ONLY place any endpoint returns one.
Global Payments / Heartland CERTIFICATION public key.
supt_… token. Filled by the Tokenize request.

request.description:
Every space type on the company, with its unit_type_id. Needed by 3 and 6.

NOTE: this endpoint's `data` is an ARRAY; every other call returns an object.

exec: // Match on NAME here only because this is the lookup that defines the ids.

request.description: The property's space groups. The public one is named 'Website Group' — match on the NAME, never 'take the first': on some properties it is last in the list.

Tiers per space type. `tier_id` is what request 4 wants as unitGroupId.

The `insurance` array here is EMPTY on every tenant — coverage comes from request 6, not this.

exec: // Prefer a tier with vacancy — request 4 only returns units for those.
const vacant = rows.find(t => t.vacant && t.vacant.count > 0) || rows[0];
const promo = rows.map(t => t.allocated_promo).find(p => p && p.id);

request.description:
Good / Better / Best for the tier. A sold-out slot comes back with unit_id and price both null.

Carries `dossier.token` (validates the price at request 7), `space_mix_id`, and the unit number at costs.Unit.number.

Not in the guide, but the quickest way to a rentable unit id and its space_mix_id.

A HELD unit disappears from this list — that is how you tell a hold took.

exec: const cheapest = units.filter(u => u.type === 'storage').sort((a, b) => a.price - b.price)[0];
console.log(`${units.length} available; picked ${cheapest && cheapest.id} (#${cheapest && cheapest.number}) at $${cheapest && cheapest.price}`);

request.description: 15 minutes. A second hold on the same unit returns inner status 409 — 'currently being held by another customer'.

exec: console.log('hold_token', r.data && r.data.hold_token, '| inner', r.status, r.msg || '');

request.description: Undocumented but works. RUN THIS if you abandon a test — otherwise the unit sits out of inventory for 15 minutes.

THE source of protection plans. Bracketed, comma-separated type ids.

Plans are per space type: ask for every type and Bellflower returns six — two storage and four Commercial — so filter by unit_type_id, never by name (a unit row says 'commercial_storage' where the plan says 'Commercial').

The money. Verified: v1 HONOURS insurance_id (adds a prorated Coverage line), start_date (details.start_date comes back as sent) and promotions.

READ `balance`, NOT `total_due`. With a promotion applied the same quote returned total_due 75.52 against balance 71.02 — total_due is the gross before discounts.

Add "token": "<dossier token from request 4>" to have Hummingbird validate the quoted price.

exec: // balance is the NET payable; total_due is gross.

request.description:
Reservation, no payment. SEPARATE journey from the rental — you do not run 8 and 10 for the same unit.

`move_in_cost` wants the guide's nested shape: {data:{rental:{amount, costs:[{amount,costType,description,start,end,total}], costType:'reservation', start, end, total}}} with UNIX timestamps. The empty object here is a placeholder.

NOT a Hummingbird call — Global Payments' own tokenizer, proving the pkapi_cert_ key works. Returns a supt_ token and the masked number.

THE CATCH: request 10 REJECTS a masked number ('Card Number is invalid') and ignores this token. Only request 9 accepts it. So this cannot currently replace a real PAN in the rental.

exec: console.log('token', j.token_value, '| masked', j.card && j.card.number, '| expires', j.token_expire);

request.description:
Generates AND signs the lease. `signed: true` means ClickWrap/Super Lease did it internally — this company is on Super Lease.

The returned documents array is required input to request 10.

cvv2 IS REQUIRED and must be a NON-EMPTY STRING: null -> 'must be a string', omitted -> 'is required', "" -> 'not allowed to be empty'.

This call accepts a MASKED card_number plus a token — but request 10 does not, so there is no point masking it here.

exec: if (d.signed === false) console.log('TRADITIONAL SIGNING — needs a signing UI; the lease call will refuse unsigned documents.');

request.description:
CREATES A REAL LEASE AND TAKES A REAL PAYMENT. The unit leaves inventory permanently.

Send hold_token for a direct rental, or reservation_id to convert a reservation — one or the other, not both.

THE RESPONSE IS NESTED UNDER `lease`, where the guide shows it flat.

TOKEN TEST RESULT (2026-08-24): sending card_number '************1111' with a supt_ token returns 500 'Card Number is invalid.' The identical payload with the real number succeeds. So this call needs the real PAN and ignores the Global Payments token.

exec: // Nested under `lease` in reality; accept flat too in case that changes.

request.description:
Takes a payment against invoices. UNLIKE request 10 it accepts a masked card_number with a token without complaint.

Omit an invoice `id` for a pre-payment; include it for a due invoice.

Expect business-logic errors while testing: 'only $0.00 due' against a settled invoice, 'an invoice with this period might already exist' for a duplicate pre-payment.

Not in the guide. Shows what actually stuck after a lease or an update.

The licence number reads back MASKED (****0103) — that is the API hiding it, not a failed write.

Not in the guide. How post-lease details get filed. PUT only — PATCH returns 405, POST 404.

PERSISTS: driver_license, _exp, _state, dob, rent_as_business, company, Addresses[] (incl. type 'mailing')
IGNORED: Military, Relationships — 200 and silently dropped
REJECTED: Vehicles — 'Vehicles[0].manufacturer is not allowed'

So military / alternate contact / vehicle must travel with request 9 instead.

Send ONLY the keys you mean to change: a present-but-empty key blanks a value.

Every document template on the property. A `super-lease` entry here means the company signs via Super Lease / ClickWrap, so request 9 returns signed: true.

GET v2/companies/{co}/documents/{id} returns the full HTML — but as an UNRENDERED Carbone template with ~320 {d.…} merge tokens, so it cannot be shown to a shopper as-is.
